content.comment_body: Hello experts, I have a simple question: If I use the new [product_name] [article_no] as a slave, is it possible to run a user program on it? I set up a small scenario with one master and two slaves, where the master receives two input bits from each slave. Communication works, I get the bits and the master program runs. However, when I try to add some logic to the slave, the connection fails. Am I making a mistake, or is a slave only able to function as additional inputs/outputs? The manual (section p.3.8.5, page 123) states: 'A [product_name] in slave mode functions as a [product_name] expansion module. No circuit program is required for slave devices. A master can read from one or more slaves.' Does this mean a user program is not needed, or not allowed, on slaves? Thank you in advance! Regards, [user_name]
Running a program on the slave is not permitted. Only the master device supports running a program, while slaves act solely as I/O expansion modules.
Thank you for clarifying. I was hoping to get more functionality from this small device!

analysis.insight_summary: The user was uncertain about whether a [product_name] configured as a slave could execute custom logic or was limited to functioning as I/O expansion. After testing and encountering issues, clarification was provided: only the master can run a user program, and slaves are strictly for input/output expansion. This interaction points out that the user manual could describe the device's capabilities more clearly to prevent confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expected to be able to execute custom logic programs on the [product_name] configured as a slave device, and not only on the master.
